chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan the last (peace be upon him)
and I said to him: The daughter of Shihab observes the days of her menstrual period, but when she performs the ritual bath (ghusl), she sees drop after drop (of blood).

He (the narrator) said: So he (the Imam) said: 'Instruct her to stand at the base of the wall just as a dog stands, then have a woman press firmly between her hips with an intense pressing, for indeed it is only something that remains in the womb called al-Iraqah, and it will all come out.'
Then he said: 'Do not inform women about this and similar things, and leave them with their impure ailment.'
He (the narrator) said: So I did to the woman what he had said, and it ceased from her, and the blood did not return to her until she died.

key_terms.أَقْرَاء: menstrual periods (plural of qar' — a term that in fiqh denotes either the period of menstruation or the period of purity, here used for the menstrual days)
key_terms.الْإِرَاقَة: al-Iraqah — a term denoting residual fluid/blood that remains in the womb after the menstrual period ends; not counted as menstrual blood proper
key_terms.غَمْز: pressing/squeezing — the physical action prescribed to expel the residual fluid
key_terms.غُسْل: ritual purification bath required after menstruation ends before resuming prayer

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS) say about drops of blood appearing after ghusl following menstruation?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS) provides a practical jurisprudential remedy for a woman who experiences persistent drops of blood after completing her menstrual period and performing ghusl. The Imam identifies this as a physiological condition called al-Iraqah — residual blood retained in the womb — and prescribes a specific posture and physical technique to expel it, confirming that the menstrual period is genuinely complete. Notably, the Imam instructs the questioner not to share this remedy with women broadly, an instruction that reflects the era's approach to specialized medical-religious knowledge and the concern that women might manipulate such knowledge to circumvent ritual obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Basry who said, 
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the last
, and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The daughter of Shihaab sat for days during her purity. But when she washed, she saw drop after the drop (of blood)’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Instruct her, so let her stand by the base of the wall just as the dog stands. Then she should instruct a woman to press between her legs with an intense pressing, for it, rather is a thing which remained in the womb, called ‘Al-Iraaqat’ and it would all be coming out’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not inform them (women) with this and with the likes of it, and leave them and their dirty ailment’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did it via the woman, that which he<sup>asws</sup> said, and it was cut off from her, and the blood (drops) did not return to her until she died’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of our people from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Basriy who has said the following:
“I once said to abu al-Hassan, the last, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that the daughter of Shihab during her Hayd- free times, after taking Ghusl (bath), finds drops after drops of discharge.
